claim: LOF ZDHHC8 mutations may elicit many of the symptoms of schizophrenia by disrupting S-palmitoylation and normal neuronal development in brain regions affected in schizophrenia.
source: These observations support a model in which LOF ZDHHC8 mutations may elicit many of the symptoms of schizophrenia by disrupting S-palmitoylation and normal neuronal development in these brain regions.
evidence: This is a hypothesis proposed by the authors based on the expression data and known disease associations.

claim: Mutations in the ZDHHC9 gene have been identified in ~2% of individuals with X-linked intellectual disability (ID).
source: Mutations in the ZDHHC9 gene, which is located on the X chromosome, have been identified in ~2% of individuals with X-linked intellectual disability (ID) (Raymond et al., 2007; Tzschach et al., 2015)
evidence: This statement is supported by citations to prior research.

claim: Neuroanatomical abnormalities reported in patients with ZDHHC9 mutations include decreased cortical, thalamic and striatal volume, as well as widespread white matter abnormalities with prominent hypoplasia of the corpus callosum.
source: Neuroanatomical abnormalities reported in patients with ZDHHC9 mutations include decreased cortical, thalamic and striatal volume, as well as widespread white matter abnormalities with prominent hypoplasia (under-development) of the corpus callosum (Baker et al., 2015; Bathelt et al., 2016)
evidence: This statement is supported by citations to prior research.

claim: Disrupted white matter integrity is thought to underlie deficits in global and local brain connectivity in patients with ZDHHC9 mutations.
source: Disrupted white matter integrity is thought to underlie deficits in global and local brain connectivity in patients with ZDHHC9 mutations (Bathelt et al., 2017)
evidence: This statement is supported by a citation to prior research.

claim: Zdhhc9 knock-out mice develop similar pathological changes to patients with ZDHHC9 mutations, including decreased volume of the corpus callosum.
source: Zdhhc9 knock-out mice also develop similar pathological changes, including decreased volume of the corpus callosum (Kouskou et al., 2018)
evidence: This statement is supported by a citation to prior research.

claim: Considerable cell-type enrichment of Zdhhc9 in oligodendrocytes was observed across studies and developmental ages.
source: We observed considerable cell-type enrichment of Zdhhc9 in oligodendrocytes across studies and developmental ages (Figure 5D and E)
evidence: This is a finding from the study's analysis of developmental expression data shown in Figure 5D and E.

claim: Zdhhc9 expression in adult mice was highly enriched in the corpus callosum.
source: Regionally, we found Zdhhc9 expression in adult mice to be highly enriched in the corpus callosum, the largest white matter tract in the brain (Figure 5F)
evidence: This is a finding from the study's analysis of regional expression data shown in Figure 5F.

claim: Disrupting S-palmitoylation in oligodendrocytes may underlie the white matter pathology and decreased connectivity observed in patients with X-linked ID and ZDHHC9 mutations.
source: As myelin production by oligodendrocytes is critical for maintaining white matter integrity, these observations indicate that disrupting S-palmitoylation in oligodendrocytes may underlie the white matter pathology and decreased connectivity observed in patients with X-linked ID and ZDHHC9 mutations.
evidence: This is a hypothesis proposed by the authors based on the expression data and known disease associations.

claim: Infantile neuronal ceroid lipofuscinosis (INCL or CLN1 disease) is a severe neurological disorder caused by LOF mutations in the PPT1 gene.
source: Infantile neuronal ceroid lipofuscinosis (INCL or CLN1 disease) is a severe neurological disorder caused by LOF mutations in the PPT1 gene that presents in the first 6–12 months of life and is characterized by rapid developmental regression, blindness and seizures, with continual deterioration until death in early childhood (Nita et al., 2016)
evidence: This statement is supported by a citation to prior research.

claim: PPT1 is thought to primarily localize to lysosomes with an essential role in lysosomal degradation of S-palmitoylated proteins.
source: While PPT1 is thought to primarily localize to lysosomes with an essential role in lysosomal degradation of S-palmitoylated proteins (Lu et al., 1996)
evidence: This statement is supported by a citation to prior research.

claim: PPT1 has a synapse-specific function in regulating synaptic vesicle cycling and synaptic transmission.
source: this protein also has a synapse-specific function in regulating synaptic vesicle cycling and synaptic transmission (Koster et al., 2021; Koster and Yoshii, 2019)
evidence: This statement is supported by citations to prior research.

claim: Neuronal Ppt1 expression was high in postnatal neurons of the spinal cord, olfactory bulb, and mid/hindbrain.
source: We found that neuronal Ppt1 expression was high in postnatal neurons of the spinal cord, olfactory bulb, and mid/hindbrain
evidence: This is a finding from the study's analysis of developmental expression data shown in Figure 5G and H.

claim: Microglia were the highest expressing non-neuronal cell type for Ppt1 at both postnatal ages.
source: while microglia were the highest expressing non-neuronal cell type at both postnatal ages (Figure 5G and H)
evidence: This is a finding from the study's analysis of developmental expression data shown in Figure 5G and H.

claim: Neurodegeneration has been detected in the spinal cord prior to onset within the brain in Ppt1 knock-out mice.
source: Neurodegeneration has been detected in the spinal cord prior to onset within the brain in Ppt1 knock-out mice, accompanied by extensive glial cell activation including microgliosis, which is a pathological hallmark of CLN1 disease (Shyng et al., 2017)
evidence: This statement is supported by a citation to prior research.

claim: Mid-/hindbrain neurons had high expression of Ppt1, consistent with reports that Ppt1 knock-out mice show early signs of brain pathology in the thalamus.
source: Mid-/hindbrain neurons also had high expression of Ppt1, consistent with reports that Ppt1 knock-out mice show early signs of brain pathology in the thalamus (Kielar et al., 2007)
evidence: This is a finding from the study's analysis of expression data shown in Figure 5G and H, with a citation supporting the interpretation.

claim: Widespread Ppt1 expression was observed in almost every brain region in adult mice.
source: Overall, we observed widespread Ppt1 expression in almost every brain region in adult mice, consistent with the sweeping neurological deficits associated with CLN1 disease (Figure 5I)
evidence: This is a finding from the study's analysis of regional expression data shown in Figure 5I.

claim: Oligodendrocyte Zdhhc9 expression increased throughout maturation, with highest expression in the myelin forming (MFOL) intermediate-maturity subtype of oligodendrocytes.
source: Examination of the Marques et al oligodendrocyte-specific scRNAseq dataset curated in BrainPalmSeq revealed that oligodendrocyte Zdhhc9 expression increased throughout maturation, with highest expression in the myelin forming (MFOL) intermediate-maturity subtype of oligodendrocytes, while slightly lower expression is maintained in mature oligodendrocytes (MOL; Figure 6A; Marques et al., 2016)
evidence: This is a finding from the study's analysis of oligodendrocyte-specific expression data shown in Figure 6A.

claim: Co-expression of HA-ZDHHC9 and FLAG-GOLGA7 increased the palmitoylated fraction of MOBP.
source: Co-expression of HA-ZDHHC9 and FLAG-GOLGA7 increased the palmitoylated fraction of MOBP and PLP1, indicating that these proteins are substrates for ZDHHC9 (Figure 6D, E and G)
evidence: This is a finding from experimental validation shown in Figure 6D and G.

claim: Co-expression of HA-ZDHHC9 and FLAG-GOLGA7 increased the palmitoylated fraction of PLP1.
source: Co-expression of HA-ZDHHC9 and FLAG-GOLGA7 increased the palmitoylated fraction of MOBP and PLP1, indicating that these proteins are substrates for ZDHHC9 (Figure 6D, E and G)
evidence: This is a finding from experimental validation shown in Figure 6E and G.

claim: CNP was not identified as a ZDHHC9 substrate in the acyl-RAC assay.
source: Conversely, CNP was not identified as a ZDHHC9 substrate in our assay (Figure 6F and G)
evidence: This is a finding from experimental validation shown in Figure 6F and G.

claim: No change in the palmitoylation of MOBP and PLP1 was observed in Zdhhc9 knock-out mice compared to wild-type.
source: While ZDHHC9 is able to palmitoylate MOBP and PLP1 in HEK cells, we observed no change in the palmitoylation of these substrates in Zdhhc9 knock-out mice (P23 half brain) compared to wild-type (Figure 6—figure supplement 2)
evidence: This is a finding from experimental validation in knockout mice shown in Figure 6—figure supplement 2.

claim: ZDHHC9 may not be required for the palmitoylation of MOBP and PLP1 in vivo due to compensation by other ZDHHC enzymes.
source: It is possible that ZDHHC9 is not required for the palmitoylation of these proteins in vivo (i.e. compensation by other ZDHHC enzymes)
evidence: This is a speculative explanation for the lack of change in knockout mice.

claim: Detection of differences in protein palmitoylation may require isolation of specific cell populations that can be diluted using whole-brain lysate.
source: or that the detection of differences in protein palmitoylation requires isolation of specific cell populations that can be diluted using whole-brain lysate as has been previously reported (Gorenberg et al., 2022; Kouskou et al., 2018)
evidence: This is a speculative explanation for the lack of change in knockout mice, supported by citations.

claim: The cell-type enrichments of ZDHHC enzymes identified in this study can be used to guide the identification of enzyme-substrate interactions.
source: Overall, these results demonstrate how the cell-type enrichments of ZDHHC enzymes identified in this study can be used, along with the lists of similarly enriched palmitoylation substrates, to guide the identification of enzyme-substrate interactions that can be further investigated in vivo.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the experimental validation results.
